query: How can we reduce incident resolution time?

per_column.name: resolution_time_hours
per_column.rationale: This is the core dependent variable for a resolution-time reduction analysis; directly derivable from opened_at and closed_at. NULLs correctly correspond to unresolved rows. Minor concern: the sampled derivation shows closed_at only, but opened_at exists in the table so the computation is well-grounded.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: Grouping resolution time by priority is a genuine analytical axis. However the original table already has a 'priority' column, making this largely redundant/a restatement. Values (High/Critical/Moderate) are a plausible normalization of the existing priority field; samples show plausible readings though not directly verifiable from the given text snippets.

per_column.name: incident_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents (Network/Database/Software/Hardware) gives a strong new axis to compare resolution times across problem classes; not directly present as a clean field ('category' is broader). The samples show sound categorization of short_description text (e.g., 'VPN'/'WiFi'->Network, 'database'->Database).

per_column.name: is_resolved
per_column.rationale: A binary resolved flag is well-grounded (derivable from state/closed_at, consistent with NULL resolution times). But it is largely redundant with the existing 'state'/'closed_at' fields and with the NULL pattern in resolution_time_hours, limiting added analytical leverage.

judge.rationale: The set centers on the correct dependent variable (resolution_time_hours) and adds a genuinely useful grouping axis (incident_type), both well suited to a 'reduce resolution time' query. priority_level and is_resolved are more grounded but partly redundant with existing columns, lowering their usefulness. Values are sound readings of the source data with no evident hallucination.
